conventions.convention: Parameters are real square-summable coefficients of minimum-norm truths in N(K)⊥. The compact operator has infinite rank, and positive singular values are indexed from 1 in nonincreasing order and tend to zero. Countable Choice is assumed.

Normalized observations satisfy Z_j = θ_j + ε s_j⁻¹ ξ_j on the product Borel space of real sequences. At ε = 0 the experiment is separately defined as the point mass at θ; white noise is not asserted to be Hilbert-space valued.
The radius Q is finite and nonnegative; weights are positive and nondecreasing, without any requirement that they diverge. The ellipsoid is not asserted to be compact.
Cutoffs belong to N₀. The estimator retains coordinates 1 through D and sets all remaining coordinates to zero; D = 0 returns the zero sequence.
Risk means expected squared ℓ² loss, rather than its square root or deterministic worst-case perturbation error. Empty variance sums equal zero.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, a fixed positive singular system for a real compact infinite-rank operator identifies minimum-norm truths with ℓ² parameters. For ε > 0, normalized observations satisfy Z_j = θ_j + ε s_j⁻¹ ξ_j with independent standard-normal coordinates; for ε = 0 the observation law is the point mass at θ.

Assume Countable Choice and ε ≥ 0. For Q ≥ 0, positive nondecreasing weights a_j, and D ∈ N₀, the exact worst-case squared sequence risk is Q²/a_{D+1}² + ε² Σ_{j=1}^D s_j⁻². The supremum is attained by (Q/a_{D+1})e_{D+1}, including Q = 0.
For Q ∈ [0,∞) and positive nondecreasing weights a_j, Θ_a(Q) consists of θ ∈ ℓ² with Σ_{j=1}^∞ a_j²θ_j² ≤ Q². No assumption that a_j tends to infinity is included.
Given z ∈ R^N and D ∈ N₀, output the finite-support sequence whose jth coordinate is z_j for 1 ≤ j ≤ D and zero for j > D. For D = 0 output the zero sequence.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit upstream choice assumption for selecting compact singular systems and applying the complete-basis coefficient identification.
The parameter space ℓ², its squared norm and coordinate vectors; nonnegative sums and finite-tail splitting.
Completeness means dense finite linear span; the model uses complete orthonormal bases of N(K)⊥ and the range closure.
The coefficient map is a bijective isometry, so every real square-summable coefficient sequence corresponds to a minimum-norm truth.
Positive singular-value indexing, complete singular systems, the compact-operator expansion, and the commuting deterministic coefficient diagram.

seams_checked.note: The fixed isonormal process and spectral-coordinate theorem supply independent standard-normal basis coordinates at positive noise. Division by positive s_j gives the stated normalized law. Zero noise is explicitly introduced separately.

The compact inverse-model definition permits noninjectivity and nonclosed range. Batch 8 explicitly adds infinite rank and restricts truths to N(K)⊥; it does not infer an everywhere-defined bounded inverse.

The source-ball identification uses the coefficient isometry and weights a_j = s_j⁻ν. The minimax comparison faithfully quotes the pointwise and worst-case squared cutoff risks, includes D = 0, and takes a square root explicitly for RMS risk.

With σ_j = s_j⁻¹, the detection definition rescales Z_j to Y_j = Z_j/σ_j = η_j + ε ξ_j and retains square-summable truth coordinates. Its additional diverging-weight assumptions strengthen the model conditions.

The SOLIT filter lemma correctly uses normalized coordinate noise σ s_j⁻¹ ξ_j; multiplying by λ_j q(λ_j) yields σ s_j q(λ_j) ξ_j. The algorithm distinguishes its unnormalized observed coordinates y_j = Y_x(u_j).
